recommended_approach: Mantaflow Liquid: FLUID modifier Domain (domain_type='LIQUID') + Flow Inflow (flow_type='LIQUID', flow_behavior='INFLOW') + Effector Collision for glass & table, then generate Liquid Mesh for close-up rendering

key_parameters.domain_settings.resolution_max: 64 (documented as a minimum for decent liquid detail; increase for close-up shots)
key_parameters.domain_settings.cache_directory: Set explicitly (e.g. env var BLENDER_CACHE_DIR or an absolute path) to ensure reliable bakes/headless operation

warnings: Domain must be large enough to contain all liquid motion during the shot (otherwise liquid will be clipped).
Low liquid resolution leads to visibly chunky/blobby surfaces; resolution_max=64 is noted as a minimum for decent detail (close-up typically needs higher).
Collision setup is sensitive for thin glass; use collision surface distance (example shown: surface_distance=0.005) and ensure the collider mesh is watertight/thick enough.
Applying modifiers via bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply is context-sensitive: object must be active and in OBJECT mode.
For automated/headless bakes, set an explicit domain_settings.cache_directory to avoid writing caches to unexpected locations.
alternative_approaches: Hybrid cheats for close-ups: animate a pouring stream mesh (curve + thickness) and use a Particle System for secondary droplets/splashes (particle Render settings like Scale Randomness/Material), reserving Mantaflow Liquid only for the glass fill/impact zone or skipping the full liquid sim entirely.
Force-field-driven particle droplets: use particle emitters and force fields (e.g., Texture force field) to art-direct splash trajectories without a full liquid solve.
